turns.question: Explain the difference between mutable and immutable Python objects. Give one bug that shared mutable state can cause.
turns.answer: Lists and dictionaries are mutable: their contents can change in place. Strings, tuples and integers are immutable. Two names can reference the same list, so appending through one name changes what the other sees. A list used as a default argument is created once and reused across calls, leaking items between calls. I use None as the default and create a fresh list inside each call.
